FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 January 1980, after the draft finalized by the Pest Control Sectional Committee had been approved by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council and the Chemical Division Council. 0.2 Carbofuran granules are used as systemic insecticides. 0.3 Carbofuran granules, encapsulated are generally manufactured to contain 8-0 percent (m/", ) of carbofuran. 0.4. In the preparation of this standard due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, t 968 and the Rules framed thereunder, However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under these, wherever applicable. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2�1960*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard,

1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of
sampling and test ror carbofuran granules, encapsulated.

2. REQUIREMENTS

2.1 Censtltuents

e - The material shall consist of technical carbofuran as the only active ingredient impregnated on suitable carrier(s) together with binder(s), stabilizer(s) and/ or other formulants.

2.1.1 Carbofuran technical, employed in the formulation of this material shall have a minimum purity of 75 percent (m/m ).
*Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised).
3

11,9360� 1980
2.2 Phyalcal - The material shall comply with the physical requirements specified In 2.2.1 to 2-2.1. 2.2.1 Description - The product .hall consist of dry, free flowing granules. free from visible extraneous matter and dust except for the amount specified ( ", 2.2.3). It may contain added colouring matter. When dusted from a granule applicator, the material .h.11 come freely without clogging or bridging the apparatus. 2.2.2 Particle Size - Not less than 97 percent by' mass of the product

shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh size of the upper declared limit and not more than 5 percent by mass of the product shall pass through a test sieve having a mesh size of lower declared limit when determined by the method described in 12.1 of IS : 6940-1973'
[ see 3.2(a) ].

2.2.2.1 The ratio of lower and upper particle sizes shall not exceed 1 : 2. 2.2.3 Dust - When determined by the method described in 12.1 of IS: 6940-1973�, not more than 1�0 percent by mass of the product shall pass through 75-micron IS Sieve [ I" IS : 460 ( Part I )-1978t].

2.2.3.1 The portion passing through this sieve shall not contain more than 8 percent by mass of the declared nominal active ingredient when determined by the method described in Appendix A. 2.2.4 Encapsulation 2.2.4.1 When material is subjected to the attrition test as described in Appendix A of IS : 9559-1980:, the residue shall not contain more than 2-0 percent by mass of declared nominal active ingredient when determined by the method described in Appendix A of this standard. 2.2.4.2 When material is subjected to the water run-off test as described in Appendix B of IS : 9359-1980:, the active ingredient in the water shall not exceed 5-0 percent by mass of the declared active ingredient when determined by the method described in Appendix A of this. standard. 2.2.5 Storage Sldilil.1 2.2.5.1 H,III stability ..... After storage at 54 ::II 2�C for 14 days, the product shall continue to comply with the requirements of 2.2.1 to 2.2.4, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. 2.2.6 Moul." C.",,,., - When determined by the method prescribed ill 4 of IS : 6940-1973�, the moisture content of the material shall not exceed 4-0 percent by mass.

3. PACKING AND MARKING

S.1 Packing - The material shall be packed as per requirements given in IS : 8190 ( Part I )-1980t. 3.2 Marking -- The containers shall bear legibly and indelibly the followin~ information and any other information as is necessary under the Ineecticfdes Act and Rules: a) Name of the material and particle size ( s,; 2.2.2 ); b) Name of the manufacturer; c) Date of manufacture; d) Batch number; e) Net mass of the contents; f) Nominal carbofuran content, percent ( m/m ); and g) The cautionary notice worded as in the Insecticides Act and
Rules.

APPENDIX

A

(Clauses 2.2.4.1, 2.2.4.2 and 2.3.1 )
DETERMINATION OF CARBOFURAN CONTENT

A-I. PRINCIPLE
A-l.1 Carbofuran on hydrolysis with glycollic potassium hydroxide liberates carbofuran phenol and allied products along with gaseous methylamine which is swept by a stream of nitrogen and absorbed in 2 percent boric acid solution. The carbofuran phenol and allied products

remain in the hydrolysis kettle as sodium salts and do not interfere in the subsequent titration. The boric acid solution titrated with decinormal hydrochloric acid estimates quantitatively liberated amine.
�Specificatlon for water for

general laboratory use (_revision ).
6

III 9360 � 1980
A�2. REAGENTS A-2.1 Glycollic Pota��lalD Hydroxide Solution -- 2 N. A-2.2 Boric Acid Solution -- 2 percent aqueous solution containing 1 ml of 0�1 percent bromocresol green indicator solution.

A-2.3 Hydrochloric Acid - 0-1 N.
A-3. APPARATUS
A-3.1 An assembly of the apparatus is illustrated in Fig. 1. Minor

modifications in the illustrative assembly with regard to joints might be made. However, it should be ensured that all joints are leak-proof. A-4. PROCEDURE A-4.1 Weigh accurately sufficient quantity of formulation to contain 0-4 to 0-6 g of the active ingredient into the reaction flask or kettle. By means of a graduated cylinder add 50 ml of the 2 N potassium hydroxide solution ( see A-2.1 ) to the kettle and assemble the apparatus as shown in the diagram. By means of a graduated cylinder add to the receiver 150 ml of 2 percent boric acid solution, Connect the nitrogen inlet tube and start the nitrogen flow so as to get slow and uniform bubbling in the receiver containing boric acid. Apply sufficient heat to the kettle so that the boric acid solution changes colour within 5-7 minutes and reflux for 60 minutes, Stop heating while continuing to pass nitrogen for the next 5 minutes, Disconnect the receiver first and then the nitrogen supply. Transfer the contents of the receiver into a 500-ml Erlenmeyer flask. Rinse the inside and outside of the ~as delivery tube and the inside of the receiver with boric acid solution, adding the washings to the Erlenmeyer flask. Titrate the content. of the Erlenmeyer flask with 0-1 N hydrochloric acid to the original colour of the boric acid solution.
A-5. CALCULATION
A-S.l Carbofuran content, percent by mass

=

22'13 x Y x N

Ii

where V .. volume of hydrochloric acid used; N = normality of the hydrochloric acid; and M = mass of sample in g taken for the test.
